newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - July 15.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian women's softball team's 1-0 victory over the United States in the finals of the prestigious Superball tournament in Columbus, Georgia, prompted coach Bob Crudgington to call his team the best in the world. The squad included eight players from the team that earned a Bronze medial at the Atlanta Olympics. Page 22.

Australian world breaststroke champion Samantha Riley led her Queensland team to victory at the inaugural Telstra Swimming League, defeating New South Wales Institute of Sport 117-79 in Sydney last night. Page 21.

Australian sprinter Melinda Gainsford-Taylor put in a significant performance of 22.23s yesterday in the 200m, breaking the Australian national record set by rival Cathy Freeman. The new record has earned Gainsford Taylor a $15,000 bonus from her personal sponsor Optus. Page 20
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

According to Olympics Minister Michael Knight, the city of Melbourne will not be involved in the Sydney 2000 games unless Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett is able to quickly confirm the viability of the $300 million Docklands Stadium as the site to host Olypic soccer games. Page 42.

The Australian women's under-20 basketball team was forced to settle for a silver medal at the world championships in Natal, Brazil, after they were defeated 78-74 in overtime yesterday. According to coach Ray Tomlinson, the team had "over-achieved" and could feel proud of themselves. Page 42.

While still unofficial, Australian racing legend Peter Brock is expected to make one last attempt to win his 10th Bathurst 1000 in the 35th annual running of the competition in October. Brock has already indicated he will race his Holden Commodore in the copycat Australian 1,000 V8 race. Page 41.
THE AGE

A less than satisfactory specialist report on his foot injury has forced Australian Football League's Essendon champion John Hird to sit out the rest of the season. Hird confirmed that he has not recovered from the stress fractures in his foot in what is bad news for the team who is currently struggling to make it into the top eight. Page B8.

The International Cricket Council has announced the use of third umpires to cover catches in the event that two field umpires are unable to come to a decision. The ICC has also approved the use of lights during normal Test-playing hours, but excludes day/night Tests situations. Page B8
Australian Football League team Carlton is expected to field rookie ruckman Mark Porter in Saturday's game against Essendon following the one-match suspension of No.1 ruckman Matthew Allen. Page B8
THE HERALD SUN

760 current and retired Australian Football League players, registered with clubs between July 1, 1993, and June 30 last year, have been formally notified by the Australian Taxation Office that they are under investigation. Page 80.

he Australian Cycling Federation has officially released the 23-rider men's squad set to represent Australia at the world road titles in Spain, to be held from October 8-12. Meanwhile, Patrick Jonkers is set to lead Australia's assault on the Tour de France today. Page 73.

According to Geelong trainer Mark Young, the Austin family which owns race horse Russian Trader will meet their lawyers in Brisbane to discuss possible legal action against champion jockey Matt Dittman. Dittman is allegedly responsible for the fatal injuies sustained by Russian Trader in last week's QTC St Leger at Eagle Farm. Page 73.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian Rugby League has released plans for a unified 16-team league next year, including a proposal to curtail the number of participating teams to 14 by 1999. The blueprint is expected to become the ARL's official position in negotiation with Suer League when the majority of club boards ratify the plan over the next two weeks. Page 68.

The Brisbane Broncos defeated the Canberra Raiders 19-4 in the Telstra Cup minor premiership last night. The Broncos beat the Raiders for the first time in five years despite a crippling injury toll and a one-sided penalty count. Page 64.

According to Australian Socceroos defender Matt Bingley, Japan does not want to play against Australia in the Asian zone World Cup Playoff. Bingley is in Japan on an 18-month contract with J-League club Kobe Vissel. Page 58.
